translations.7d2464280b86943d: Source code and resources for the shared system used by Unisaki Studio's posing tools.
translations.c040aee682c09a53: To check the installed version, select the posing tool in Unity and look at the top of its Inspector. Instructions are in the package README.
translations.5deb981a6d80df41: ## This repository and the terms of use
translations.b333e3f69aa43084: The source code and resources in this repository are not open source. You must purchase the product on BOOTH and agree to its terms of use.
translations.88d9253fa14db58d: [Terms of use](Packages/jp.unisakistudio.posingsystem/ゆにさきポーズシステム利用規約（日本語版）.pdf)
translations.3384667be43ce486: The shared posing system used by Kawaii Posing Tool, Cool Posing Tool and related products. It uses Modular Avatar and NDMF to generate the required menus and animations when you upload an avatar.
translations.37b1b586e6f00193: This README covers v3.2.0, currently in development. A release date has not been set. Check the installed version at the top of the posing tool's Inspector. See also [new features and changelog](CHANGELOG.md).
translations.f057ec94623ab83e: Choose a display language with Language / 言語 at the top of the Inspector. One selection controls both the Inspector and generated VRChat menu. Re-upload the avatar to change its in-game language.
translations.6c7e34186b56734a: Without a saved choice, the tool follows the computer's language and uses English for unsupported languages. This works on Windows, macOS and Linux. The last selection is saved in EditorPrefs and reused in other projects belonging to the same OS user on this computer. An explicit selection already saved on an avatar is preserved. Preferences do not sync to other computers. License storage is unchanged.
translations.ef58b910342a4f74: Choose a README, changelog or manual from the bundled [language index](Documentation~/Localization/index.html). The Inspector's Manual and View changelog also follow the selected language. Original agreements and reference translations remain separately available.
translations.3240210502334b10: The delay before the selected pose takes effect when switching between standing, crouching and sitting in desktop mode has been reduced. This applies to normal builds and prebuilds, with no special command or extra setting. Existing behavior is retained in VR mode and special states. Update older prebuilds before uploading.
translations.0eb826cefdff818a: Follow the purchased product's installation instructions and add the posing tool using VCC or ALCOM. This system is installed as a dependency of the posing tool.
translations.aa0e93c49ca876d3:
- A Unity 2022.3 VRChat avatar project
- VRChat Avatars SDK 3.10.4 or later
- Modular Avatar 1.x, version 1.15.1 or later
- NDMF (Non-Destructive Modular Framework) 1.x, version 1.14.0 or later
translations.fc547ae5cc8c18cd: For Kawaii Posing Tool, update the product to 3.2.0 in ALCOM / VCC and check that Unisaki Posing System is also 3.2.0. If you use prebuilds, click Update prebuild and save the scene before uploading the avatar.
translations.064a37c64aaa4128: Cool Posing Tool 1.2.0 uses shared system 3.2.0. Update the product and shared system together to compatible versions.
translations.810eb63597d533a4: New installations now use the regular Prefab. Turn off unneeded items under Features to reduce parameter usage. Select Pose alone uses a base of 8 bit.
translations.868cf18738a90d19: The old 8bit Prefabs remain in each product's Editor/Legacy folder to preserve references from existing avatars and presets. You can keep using an existing 8bit edition without deleting or replacing its Prefab. The Unity menu no longer offers the 8bit edition for new installations.
translations.6ef562436dd6f663: In the Hierarchy, select the tool object inside the avatar, such as 可愛いポーズ or カッコいいポーズ, to configure it.
translations.db11f5b7a2a1a0d7:
| Tab | Settings |
| --- | --- |
| Features | In-game menu features, convenience features, icon images and ExpressionParameters usage |
| Poses | Select, add and reorder poses; preview in the Scene; pose details and animation adjustment |
| Avatar Setup | Body-specific correction, knee correction, original/custom motion imports and presets |
translations.3c03db36ebfa6a46: For items with detailed settings, click Open settings to expand the controls below. Breathing settings are also under Features.
translations.ef7802d53ffe53c1: Use Help / Changelog at the top to open the manual, support or changelog. Switch between the product and Unisaki Posing System when reading the changelog.
translations.7abe60caa96b545e: Items enabled under Features > Menu features appear in the in-game menu. For example, enabling Mirror adds a control to switch mirroring in VRChat. Checking it in the Inspector does not make every pose permanently mirrored.
translations.bddece415aadd3f2:
| Feature | Additional bit usage |
| --- | ---: |
| Mirror | 1 bit |
| Disable Gestures | 1 bit |
| Animate breathing | 0 bit |
| Breathing (in-game ON/OFF) | 1 bit |
| Foot Height | 8 bit |
| Floor Height | 8 bit |
| Photo Mode (local display only) | 0 bit |
| Sync Photo Mode | 16 bit |
| Keep your head visible in Photo Mode | 0 bit |
| Disable VRChat idle sway | 0 bit |
| Reduce pose distortion from head rotation | 1 bit (shared with Roll Over) |
| Roll Over | 10 bit (including 1 bit shared with pose-distortion reduction) |
translations.86be79bc5a102629: Roll Over uses 1 bit for ON/OFF, 8 bit for head tilt and 1 bit for head lock. If pose-distortion reduction is already enabled, adding Roll Over costs an additional 9 bit. Shared parameters are counted once; the display updates as you change the checkboxes.
translations.7496dd3b030e5bc0: The displayed total covers the posing tools installed on that avatar. It is not the avatar's overall total including clothing and other gimmicks. Shared settings are counted once even when multiple posing tools are installed. If the pose count exceeds the basic index range, pose selection can also require additional bits.
translations.4e2acdd51f81bc24:
- Foot Height adjusts the feet side while keeping the head position. Use it to align the feet with a floor or bed.
- Floor Height moves the whole body, including the head, vertically. 50% is the original height, 0% is 3m below and 100% is 3m above. The default is 50%.
translations.8ce73c604a564659: Both are under Settings in the in-game menu; Floor Height follows Foot Height. Move Floor Height away from the center to move vertically. Return near 50% to restore the original height and end the correction. There is no separate floating ON/OFF switch. Viewpoint correction occurs when floating starts and while adjusting floor height.
translations.9bcdf69a52e1b232: For regular animations, Foot Height no longer duplicates whole-body motion data to adjust height. This reduces generated animation data; it does not reduce every avatar's total size to one third.
translations.769f88ffabb12209:
1. Enable Features > Menu features > Photo Mode.
2. In VRChat, open Photo Mode and select a pose under Select Pose.
3. Use Distance to move up to 3m forward and Direction to turn the avatar. At distances above 0, the avatar faces you.
4. Enable Lock Feet if needed. It is not forced on at startup, so you can position the avatar before locking. If Disable Gestures is included in the menu, you can also change hand shapes on the same screen.
5. Exit Photo Mode resets distance and rotation and releases foot lock.
translations.2d309b91454d5538: Photo Mode movement and rotation use 0 bit when visible only on your screen. To show the position and rotation to others, enable Convenience > Sync Photo Mode. Distance and rotation together use 16 bit.
translations.1e2828b934ad2d60: If your avatar's head disappears when it is nearby, enable Convenience > Keep your head visible in Photo Mode. This affects only your local display during Photo Mode and returns to normal when it ends.
translations.81f470a45fcbcdc8: When both back-lying and front-lying poses are selected, jump in place to switch between them. If only one is selected, the avatar keeps that posture. To disable jump switching, turn off Switch lying posture by jumping under Features > Convenience in Unity. This adds 0 bit of synchronized parameter usage. If the avatar has multiple posing tools, disabling it in any one applies to the whole avatar.
translations.106dc56595373d52: In supported lying poses, tilting your head sideways smoothly rolls the body. Not every lying pose supports this automatically.
translations.ce8d6b30dc0f88ec:
1. Enable Features > Menu features > Roll Over.
2. Under Poses, open Details for the lying pose and enable Enable roll over.
3. Assign a side-lying animation to Sideways roll-over pose. The original and side-lying poses are used to generate rolls in both directions. Adjust Ground correction strength if needed.
4. In VRChat, select a supported pose and enable Roll Over. Release head lock before using it.
translations.1aeced6549aa7ed2: When Roll Over is enabled for a pose, head tilt determines the animation's playback position, so normal MotionTime settings are unavailable. To use a complete roll-over animation, assign it to the regular animation field and leave Sideways roll-over pose empty. Prepare an animation with the left side at playback position 0, back-lying at 0.5 and the right side at 1.
translations.7378ada9fd45ff21: Features > Convenience > Animate breathing adds breathing motion to the chest and other parts. Open settings lets you choose None, Weak, Medium, Strong, Rapid or Custom for each posture category. Rapid uses faster breathing. Custom lets you assign your own breathing animation.
translations.035eb41021567955: Breathing animation alone uses 0 bit. To stop or resume it in VRChat, also enable Menu features > Breathing. Synchronizing ON/OFF uses 1 bit. Changing the intensity does not increase bit usage.
translations.73d6b9fa21a58416: The neck, shoulders and arms move with the chest to reduce head and hand displacement. Their positions are not perfectly fixed, so choose an intensity suited to the body shape and pose.
translations.edd1b2ff7c7133d3: Convenience > Disable VRChat idle sway reduces the idle body sway applied by VRChat. It defaults to off and preserves the posing tool's breathing and other custom motions. It can be enabled without breathing and uses no additional bits. It does not stop movement caused by something other than the default idle animation.
translations.ebc17b91aa6199bd: With multiple posing tools, enabling idle-sway suppression in any one affects the whole avatar. To restore it, turn this setting off in every tool and re-upload.
translations.bcd2fffdde5b82e8: ### Reduce pose distortion from head rotation
translations.a5ac9813282e3d14: Use this if releasing head lock distorts a pose because the neck orientation differs from the original pose. It is under Features > Convenience and does not add an in-game menu entry. While head lock is active, the original pose's orientation is used. Back-lying poses are excluded to preserve their original upward-facing orientation.
translations.972ae159d42c5165:
- Generate pose icons creates images of the avatar in each pose for the menu. This makes poses easier to recognize but adds image-generation time to the build.
- Reduce icon size lowers the image resolution to reduce avatar size.
translations.a3b85fa920925ea4: Pose icons are not generated for Android builds. Use Retake icons after changing clothing or appearance. Use Update pose thumbnails to refresh the pose-list images. These operations take time; read the confirmation dialog before proceeding.
translations.678ba0d2101fa329: Choose a posture category on the left of Poses. The magnifying-glass tab at the top searches pose names across categories. Details groups the animation, icon, MotionTime and other settings.
translations.7c14e655c29a3ace: To add multiple animations, drag them into the add area, or select them in the Project window and click Load selected clips from Project. Duplicate clips are excluded.
translations.a026d8bf14122ea5: To reorder a pose, choose its destination under Details > Order. The up/down buttons are also available. Moving a pose preserves whether its details are expanded.
translations.650b99fac5995dcc: Click Preview for a pose to inspect it in the Scene without opening the adjustment window. Ending the preview restores the original display. This quick preview does not run MA or NDMF builds, so it can differ from the final clothing or FloorAdjuster result assembled during a build. Check the final clothing and ground contact after building the avatar as well.
translations.3c79f05aae20a26e: ## Animation adjustment and automatic limb adjustment (IK)
translations.f1b4cb7aa3381e0d: Open Animation adjustment under Poses to adjust the body and limbs while previewing. Save the adjustment animation using the window's save controls when finished.
translations.fd662974ae23df47: Supported products and poses use automatic limb adjustment to fit limb positions to the avatar's body. Use Enable automatic limb adjustment in the animation adjustment window for the overall setting and Enable IK for this pose for individual poses. Poses without automatic adjustment are identified as such.
translations.cdaa337a7b96a497: To finish the automatic result by hand, click Bake IK into adjustments. This writes the current IK result to a new adjustment animation and disables IK for that pose on that avatar. The original animation is preserved. The button is available when overall and per-pose automatic adjustment are enabled and usable IK settings exist.
translations.96491da66613749b: Under Avatar Setup, Prevent reverse knee bending toggles knee correction. Set Minimum knee bend (degrees) in its details. Enable avatar correction is available when compatible correction data exists. Corrections that overlap with automatic limb adjustment may not be usable together.
translations.d50fef0dce536f27: ## Original poses, custom motions and presets
translations.49ada2ae37af40ea:
- Use original standing, crouching and prone poses automatically imports the poses originally assigned to the avatar.
- Use your own motions opens import settings to assign a motion separately for each type, such as standing, Crouching or Prone. Normally, assign one motion per type.
- Integrate tracking locks with other tools can be enabled if the locking features do not work correctly alongside other gimmicks.
translations.446593edb3966c9b: Manually assigning motions in the import settings is separate from automatically importing the avatar's original poses.
translations.4a5b5b615ce12e70: Presets are at the bottom of the tab. Search by name and click Apply this preset to replace the pose settings. Presets are primarily a starting configuration for installation. They replace current settings, so save any existing adjustments before switching.
translations.e3e06f99b48bdc04: Displaying the preset list loads only names and supported-avatar information. Adjustment animations are loaded when the selected preset is applied. Even the first listing does not preload animations for every avatar.
translations.64e90697af81f8c9: The list is grouped into Compatible with avatar, User-created and Unisaki Studio official. Hide bundled presets is a shared display preference within the project. Adding, editing or deleting presets refreshes the list. Click Reload if the display has not updated.
translations.0c801e40c7f213c8: With Use original standing, crouching and prone poses enabled, motions are detected from the avatar's Base each time data is generated. Detection does not write back to the manual import settings, so automatically imported types remain unassigned in that list. Changes to Base motions or automatic-import ON/OFF take effect at the next generation.
translations.13047efed776d740: Automatic imports at upload time apply to the build copy. They do not modify the original scene object, import settings, source Controller or motions. An existing prebuild is reused when its inputs have not changed.
translations.f517692ddf9c2c61: A type with a manual assignment uses that setting, including rotation, adjustment animation and playback-position settings. Turning Use off or removing an assigned motion stops automatic import for that type. Clear manual selection removes that type's settings and adjustments; if automatic import is enabled, the next generation detects it again. This operation supports Undo. If multiple legacy settings exist for one type, the valid setting selected in the Inspector takes precedence.
translations.aaf3a878e9816116: Settings added to the list by older automatic-import versions cannot be distinguished from manually registered or adjusted settings and are not automatically deleted. Use Clear manual selection only for types you want to return to automatic import. With multiple products on an avatar, manual settings in the other products also affect the shared original poses.
translations.bc8b80681785c165: Prebuilds reuse generated data to shorten avatar builds. Create or refresh them with Update prebuild. Normal avatar builds also generate the necessary data, so you do not need to prebuild manually every time.
translations.62dafc8edf1a6c2c: Changing settings marks the prebuild as needing an update. Check settings at the top of the Inspector and the Hierarchy markers notify you. Refreshing the prebuild after changing poses or IK settings reduces subsequent build time.
translations.fb6cd08fc751a6dd: Warning display settings are inside Check settings. You can hide individual warning types or Hierarchy markers. Hiding a warning does not fix its cause or refresh generated data. Errors and required generation still apply.
translations.3f86d01d52453bac:
- Intended for three-point tracking and desktop use. Pose locking during full-body tracking is unsupported.
- Body shape and avatar modifications may require further adjustments to limb contact or clothing.
- Special Base layers or other pose-changing gimmicks may prevent the intended behavior.
- Photo Mode movement/rotation and Floor Height correct tool poses and the default/custom motions used when no tool pose is selected. Check the actual VRChat client for replaced default motions and viewpoint behavior.
translations.02ed399a8dfddbfe: The source code and resources in this repository are not open source. Use requires a legitimate product purchase and agreement to the [bundled terms of use](ゆにさきポーズシステム利用規約（日本語版）.pdf).
translations.e8ae46c0808b3167: When reporting an issue, include the product and Unisaki Posing System versions; Unity, VRChat SDK, Modular Avatar and NDMF versions; avatar used; reproduction steps; and Console error details.
translations.79fec8d04d3cf763:
- Added thirty-language display for the Inspector, editing actions, installation dialogs, standard pose names and generated VRChat menus.
- Unified language selection for the Inspector and in-game menu. The default follows the computer's language, and the last choice is reused in other projects belonging to the same OS user.
- README, changelog and offline manuals can be opened in the selected language.
- Prepared display names for all 128 standard poses and feature descriptions using the established terminology.
translations.25d84bc9d3caff87: - Existing avatar settings, custom names, asset references, parameter identifiers and license storage are preserved.
translations.26e3fc73d9977c89:
- Fixed the face remaining tilted upward after getting up from a prone pose when Reduce pose distortion from head rotation was enabled.
- Head lock can now be toggled under Settings > Automatic head lock when supine in the EX menu even when Foot Height is disabled. Avatars where the item disappeared in 3.1.0 or 3.1.1 regain it when built after updating.
- Update prebuild now works even when the avatar itself is unchecked in Unity.
- Fixed pose generation sometimes failing after an update if an older shared posing Controller remained in Assets. User-edited Controller settings are also carried over.
- When the tool or a parent is disabled and the shared posing Animator cannot be used, the affected object's name is shown. Open it with Check settings > Select target.
- When a prebuild shows Settings changed, use Details > Review changes since saving to see which settings differ from the previous build.
- If script errors stop the build (PS050), up to 5 original Unity errors are shown. Ask about this error opens a draft containing Unity/tool versions and the error code for you to review, edit and send.
translations.5b848fae7ca7403a: If you use prebuilds, click Update prebuild after updating, save the scene, then build and upload the avatar again.
translations.8e9e9b2a682e7cca:
- Enabled Floor Height and Roll Over entries now appear under Settings in the VRChat EX menu even when Mirror is disabled.
- Correct roll-over settings are carried over for Legs Out (足伸ばし), Relaxed (リラックス) and One Knee Up (膝立て) even if an older version's poses were reordered, deleted or renamed. Fully unpacked objects are supported when the original pose can be identified. Custom poses, explicitly disabled roll-over settings and replacement side-lying motions are preserved.
- Fixed a brief prone pose when selecting an avatar in VRChat. Also fixed a brief supine pose when jumping with only a prone pose selected. Jump switching can be disabled under Features > Convenience > Switch lying posture by jumping; it defaults to on.
- If an update breaks a reference to the shared posing Animator Controller, a warning is shown and the Controller is rebuilt from settings when recovery is possible. References to Controllers shared by multiple avatars are preserved.
- Projects with compilation errors now stop at the start of the build with guidance about the cause. Automatic cleanup of generated Controllers is deferred while script errors prevent checking references.
- Adding a tool prioritizes its official Prefab even if another Prefab with the same product name exists in the project. Prebuilds can continue when shared Controllers differ only in line endings.
- Write Defaults on FX layers added by the posing tool, including Floor Height, now follows the avatar's settings.
translations.bb3e9468e4514bac: If you use prebuilds, click Update prebuild on the scene's tool after updating, save the scene, then build and upload the avatar again.
translations.09cfa86c5703dce4:
- Added automatic limb adjustment (IK) for supported poses, avatar-specific correction and prevention of backward knee bending.
- Photo Mode adjusts avatar position and rotation, with optional synchronization and visibility of your own head during photography.
- Floor Height moves the entire body vertically by up to 3m and can be used separately from Foot Height.
- Added breathing motion, suppression of default idle sway and reduction of pose distortion caused by neck orientation.
- The Inspector shows enabled features and parameter usage. Added pose search, batch addition, reordering and quick Scene previews.
- Sped up switching between standing, crouching and sitting in desktop mode.
- Improved prebuild warnings after settings changes, Inspector scrolling overhead and long stalls during generated-data cleanup.
- Fixed unchanged prebuilds being flagged for an update and regenerated on upload when automatic import was enabled. Imported results apply to the generated avatar without changing the original object's import settings.
- Added head-tilt roll over and per-pose motion settings.
- Improved migration of old preset roll-over settings, custom motion imports and generated-asset management.
translations.97ee69044f86beb5:
- Added fixed length and the Head-to-Viewpoint vertical (Y) and front/back (Z) differences as IK position-length references.
- Inspector warnings also appear to the left of object names in the Hierarchy, covering missing/stale prebuilds and current motion-import or preset-operation warnings.
- Fixed Unity stalling for a long time when automatic generated-data cleanup on scene opening loaded generated Controllers from other scenes.
- Fixed prebuild history disappearing after changing poses or features. The display now says settings have changed since the prebuild rather than Not run, with a matching Hierarchy update warning.
- Shared prebuild comparison results between the Inspector and Hierarchy to reduce scrolling overhead while settings and referenced assets are unchanged. Builds still compare every time.
translations.f0d251c991ceb466:
- Changed normal desktop posture switching to a single-evaluation approach for regular builds and prebuilds. VR and special conditions retain their existing paths.
- Prebuilds from alpha.3 or earlier are recognized as needing an update.
- Preserved the viewpoint when changing floor height during photography, then restored the latest floor height when photography ends.
translations.aa6273b5dac43a49:
- Automatic import now detects motions only during generation, without adding or modifying manual import settings in prebuilds/builds.
- Automatic-import ON/OFF, Base changes and removal of manual overrides now trigger regeneration. Shared manual assignments/adjustments across products are preserved, and obsolete imported motions return to the default posture.
- Generated prebuild Controllers are managed in one file per avatar and scene GUID. Shared references from duplicates, other scenes or Prefabs are separated before updating.
- Builds use NDMF's temporary asset management and do not add editable generated files.
- Generated data is checked when scenes open or are saved. Unsaved edits, Undo/Redo data and external references are retained; only clearly owned unused files are moved to the recycle bin.
- Imported motion rotation, adjustment animations and playback positions are applied. Rotation, RootT/RootQ and Humanoid adjustments use the same processing as regular poses.
- Nested BlendTree adjustments are copied for the import destination, preserving the original motion and walking blend settings.
- Standing-only playback positions are expanded into static poses at the original frame rate without stopping playback on the walking side.
translations.6127d86dd7618c9a:
- Photo Mode and Floor Height correction also apply to default/custom motions when no tool pose is selected.
- Expanded Floor Height to 3m up/down. 50% is now the original height and default, 0% is 3m below and 100% is 3m above.
- Fixed Standing-only overrides modifying the source BlendTree.
- Poses without IK rules use manual correction and no longer show unnecessary generation warnings.
- Fixed adjustment drafts being confused between identically named poses and motion changes inside the same asset being missed.
- Fixed an invalid initial-pose index selecting another pose.
- Unsupported AnimatorOverrideController imports now show guidance instead of throwing an exception.
- Applying old presets preserves explicitly disabled roll-over settings.
- Improved feature icon visibility in the light Editor theme.
translations.03d001b7e48d8f6c: VRChat client checks of viewpoint behavior and replaced default motions remain in progress.
translations.ffbd42873d123ec1:
- Added per-feature ON/OFF and ExpressionParameters usage display.
- Added Photo Mode to move the avatar forward and rotate it.
- Added optional Photo Mode synchronization: 0 bit locally, 16 bit synchronized.
- Added an option to keep your avatar's head visible during Photo Mode.
- Added Floor Height to move the whole body, including the head, up/down by 3m. 50% is the original height and default, 0% is 3m below and 100% is 3m above.
- Added head-tilt roll over and per-pose animation settings.
- Added breathing motion with Weak, Medium, Strong, Rapid and Custom settings.
- Breathing motion and its in-game ON/OFF menu can be selected separately: 0 bit for motion alone, 1 bit for synchronized ON/OFF.
- Added suppression of VRChat's default idle sway.
- Added reduction of pose distortion caused by neck-orientation differences.
- Added automatic limb adjustment (IK) for supported poses, with overall and per-pose ON/OFF.
- Added Bake IK into adjustments to save IK results to an adjustment animation.
- Added avatar-specific pose correction, prevention of backward knee bending and minimum bend angle settings.
- Added quick pose previews in the Scene from the pose list.
- Added category tabs, cross-category search, batch animation addition and destination-order selection.
- Added product and shared-system changelogs within the Inspector.
translations.f26bc41975798f76:
- Sped up preset loading to shorten waits when adding tools or displaying presets.
- Adding, editing or deleting presets automatically updates the list.
- Organized the Inspector into Features, Poses and Avatar Setup tabs.
- Added setting descriptions and icons and standardized expandable details.
- Moved breathing details into Features and presets to the bottom of Avatar Setup.
- Separated manual custom-motion assignments from automatic original-pose imports.
- Reduced duplicated whole-body animation data generated for foot-height adjustment.
- Pose image updates now use a button with a confirmation dialog.
- Grouped warning display settings inside Check settings.
- Removed new installation of dedicated 8bit Prefabs in favor of feature selection on regular Prefabs. Existing references are preserved.
- Raised the minimum VRChat Avatars SDK version to 3.10.4.
translations.e5a1c621cea8b787:
- Photo Mode and Floor Height correction now also cover default/custom motions when no tool pose is selected.
- Fixed Standing-only overrides modifying the source BlendTree.
- Poses without valid IK rules use manual adjustments and avoid unnecessary IK generation warnings.
- Fixed adjustments mixing between identically named poses and replacements of motions within one asset not triggering regeneration.
- A disabled initial-pose index no longer selects another pose if reused.
- Unsupported AnimatorOverrideController imports of original poses now show guidance instead of an exception.
- Applying old presets preserves explicitly disabled roll-over settings.
- Improved Inspector icon backgrounds so feature icons remain identifiable in the light Editor theme.
translations.70022d27ececae44:
- Fixed missing Roll Over, Floor Height and Photo Mode icons when adding a tool to an avatar.
- Fixed loss of supported poses' roll-over settings when applying old presets.
- Fixed name editing moving to another pose when opening different details.
- Fixed pose details closing after reordering and corrected settings Undo/Redo handling.
- Fixed previews overlapping the original avatar or adding placement offsets twice.
- Fixed preview errors on avatars with missing components.
- Fixed IK limb orientation/position offsets caused by avatar bone orientation or scale differences.
- Fixed warnings and prebuild status not updating immediately after settings changes.
- Fixed reuse of stale prebuilds after changing IK settings.
- Fixed build errors when generating additional features in some configurations.
translations.25370ce74f52fa32:
## [3.0.16] - 2026-09-14
- Raised the minimum NDMF dependency to 1.14.0 because the system uses the `VirtualAnimatorController.SetParameter` API.
translations.2bceec03b2601f37:
## [3.0.15] - 2026-09-13

translations.bde03f8de5a5c0e9:

- Fixed the Disable Gestures entry disappearing for the second and subsequent posing tools on the same avatar.
- Fixed USSPS_Locomotion sometimes returning to Standing even when a posture such as SleepDown was selected.
- Fixed pose height and X/Z offsets when using FloorAdjuster, accounting for processing order in both the MA and AAO editions.
- Generated prebuilt AnimatorControllers that have been deleted now recover automatically to the standard PosingSystem_Locomotion.
- Fixed build errors when every standing pose had been removed.
- Presets are now listed in avatar-name order.
translations.8d787c3df8e46130:
## [3.0.13] - 2026-09-04
- Fixed unstable posture recovery caused by a standing self-transition when returning to standing immediately after beginning to crouch in VR mode.
translations.f9093a84a80b4164:

- Fixed tools without a prebuild being incorrectly marked as having changed settings during an NDMF build.
- Fixed `AddAssetToSameFile` failures caused by adding generated assets to a temporary AnimatorController during an NDMF build.
translations.21c3434aaa4ba4e4:
## [3.0.11] - 2026-08-31
- Fixed processing failures caused by the prebuild avatar's Scene becoming invalid in NDMF 1.14.7 and later.
- Fixed `MissingReferenceException` when the NDMF error display referenced a destroyed LocalizationAsset.
translations.eb355a78e25501c0:

translations.63ac3178b7280bc1: A VRChat pose-locking tool for cute sitting and lying poses with three-point tracking or desktop mode. Includes 85 poses: 15 standing, 20 crouching, 17 sitting, 16 front-lying and 17 back-lying.

translations.f9631a2ac8eb42c9:
- Photo Mode: move the avatar up to 3m forward and adjust its rotation. Uses 0 bit locally, or 16 bit to show position and rotation to others.
- Head visibility during photography: prevent your nearby avatar's head from disappearing specifically during Photo Mode.
- Floor Height: move the whole body, including the head, up/down by 3m. 50% is the original height and default, 0% is 3m below and 100% is 3m above. This is separate from Foot Height, which moves the feet side while preserving head position.
- Roll Over: tilt your head to roll left/right in supported lying poses.
- Breathing: add breathing motion to the chest and other parts, with None, Weak, Medium, Strong, Rapid and Custom settings for each posture category.
- Disable VRChat idle sway: suppress default idle sway while retaining the tool's breathing and other custom motions.
- Reduce pose distortion from head rotation: reduce distortion when releasing head lock if the neck orientation differs from the original pose.
- Feature selection: include only the required in-game menu features and check ExpressionParameters usage in the Inspector.
- Pose search, batch addition and reordering: search across categories, load multiple clips and select destination order.
- Quick Scene previews: use Preview in the pose list to inspect the posture in place.
translations.783af266ca7af2e4: - Automatic limb adjustment (IK): fit supported poses' limb positions to the avatar's body. Includes per-pose ON/OFF and baking the result into adjustment animations.
translations.ed136af5b95f5dab: ### Roll over with the included poses
translations.98c6c7d3235fc9a5: The back-lying poses Legs Out, Relaxed and One Knee Up include side-lying settings for roll over. Their rolls are based respectively on 横向き寝, Nap and Cat Nap.
translations.7fedec56ab7874fd: Enable Features > Menu features > Roll Over and upload. In VRChat, select a supported pose and Roll Over. Release head lock before use.
translations.be2a739200d22f0f: To configure it yourself, enable Poses > Details > Enable roll over and assign an animation to Sideways roll-over pose. Normal MotionTime settings are unavailable for a pose using Roll Over.
translations.0fd74bbc9d26400b: The included automatic limb adjustment is available, although not every pose needs IK. Use Enable automatic limb adjustment in the animation adjustment window for the overall setting and Enable IK for this pose for individual poses.
translations.784d00cc1b3d2440: Bake IK into adjustments writes the current automatic result to a new adjustment animation and disables IK for the pose, allowing further manual work. It is available when overall and per-pose automatic adjustment are enabled and applicable IK settings exist.
translations.8424f6e3d41f09e5: Avatar Setup also provides Prevent reverse knee bending and its detailed Minimum knee bend (degrees) setting.
translations.c64a834af3a8c6bd:
1. Download the files from the product page at the store where you purchased it.
2. Import the bundled 可愛いポーズツール.unitypackage into Unity to register the license and package repositories.
3. In VCC or ALCOM, add Kawaii Posing Tool and Modular Avatar to your Unity project. The shared Unisaki Posing System and NDMF are also installed as dependencies.
4. Right-click the target avatar in the Hierarchy and choose Unisaki Studio > Add Kawaii Posing.
5. Select the added 可愛いポーズ object inside the avatar and configure the desired features and poses in the Inspector.
6. Upload the avatar normally.

translations.b4e1669a45146eed:
- Breathing motion uses 0 bit. Only Menu features > Breathing, used to stop/resume it in-game, costs 1 bit for synchronized ON/OFF.
- Photo Mode uses 0 bit locally. Convenience > Sync Photo Mode uses 16 bit. Keep your head visible in Photo Mode uses 0 bit.
- Foot Height and Floor Height each use 8 bit. Move Floor Height away from the center to move vertically; return near 50% to end correction.

translations.bdaa7964fc60d9df:
- Select poses in each category through the Expressions menu. In VR, head height switches standing, crouching, sitting and lying postures.
- While lying, face orientation switches back/front lying. When both poses are selected, jumping in place also switches them. Disable this under Features > Convenience > Switch lying posture by jumping in Unity (enabled by default). Adjust category-switching heights using the thresholds in Settings.
- On desktop, use C and Z to change posture. If Z does not reach a lying pose, raise the lying-height threshold in Settings.
- Disable Gestures uses the hand shapes assigned to the pose instead of controller finger gestures.
- Foot Height adjusts the feet side while preserving head position. Floor Height moves the whole body, including the head, vertically. They appear in that order in Settings.
- Moving forward with Photo Mode > Distance turns the avatar toward you. Use Direction to turn it and enable Lock Feet when ready. Exit Photo Mode restores distance/rotation and releases foot lock.
- Breathing is available when breathing animation is enabled. Set intensity in Unity and switch it ON/OFF in-game.

translations.4c66fbb298e8e9c2:

- Foot Height and Floor Height each use 8 bit. Move Floor Height away from the center to move the whole body vertically; return near 50% to end correction.
- Roll Over alone uses 10 bit. It shares 1 bit with Reduce pose distortion from head rotation, so enabling both still totals 10 bit.
- Mirror and Disable Gestures each use 1 bit.
translations.52daca6e247fc4ad:
- Select poses in each category through the Expressions menu. In VR, head height switches standing, crouching, sitting and lying postures.
- While lying, face orientation switches back/front lying. With both selected, jumping also switches them; disable this under Features > Convenience > Switch lying posture by jumping. Adjust category-switching heights using the thresholds in Settings.
- On desktop, use C and Z to change posture. If Z does not reach a lying pose, raise the lying-height threshold in Settings.
- Disable Gestures uses the hand shapes assigned to the pose instead of controller finger gestures.
- Foot Height adjusts the feet side while preserving head position. Floor Height moves the whole body, including the head, vertically. They appear in that order in Settings.
- Moving forward with Photo Mode > Distance turns the avatar toward you. Use Direction to turn it and enable Lock Feet when ready. Exit Photo Mode restores distance/rotation and releases foot lock.
- Breathing is available when breathing animation is enabled. Set intensity in Unity and switch it ON/OFF in-game.
translations.6295b7b8bed5c017:

translations.f675a3d502bd6e37: # Kawaii Posing Tool — English User Guide
translations.240461debb7fb962: Kawaii Posing provides 85 poses for desktop and three-point VR: 15 standing, 20 crouching/chair, 17 floor-sitting, 17 back-lying, and 16 front-lying poses.
translations.4b4ce8f2136c0a4d: This guide covers installation, avatar setup, VRChat controls, pose editing, updates, and troubleshooting. The purchased ZIP includes `START_HERE.html` for the quickest route to installation.
translations.6ae60319e9c41d31:
- Use a Unity 2022.3 VRChat **avatar** project created or managed with VRChat Creator Companion (VCC) or ALCOM.
- Required packages: VRChat Avatars SDK 3.10.4 or later; Modular Avatar 1.x, version 1.15.1 or later; and NDMF 1.x, version 1.14.0 or later.
- The tool is for Humanoid avatars in desktop mode and three-point VR (headset and two controllers). Pose locking while full-body tracking is active is unsupported.
- Back up an existing project before installing or updating. Finish any outstanding Unity compile errors first.
- The installer downloads the product and dependencies from their package repositories. An internet connection is required. Avatar models, VRChat SDK, Modular Avatar, and NDMF are not included in this ZIP.
translations.07d7ee924d86344a:
1. Extract the entire ZIP into a normal folder outside your Unity project.
2. Open the intended avatar project in Unity. Import `Installer/KawaiiPosing_Installer.unitypackage` using **Assets > Import Package > Custom Package**, or open the file with Unity.
3. Read the import and installation prompts. The license confirmation explains which product licenses will be installed. Use **Language...** (or **言語…**) in a confirmation dialog to change the installer language.
4. Confirm license installation. The license also covers the shared Unisaki Posing System used by this product. The installer can offer to remove its own setup files afterward; this cleanup does not remove the installed product license.
5. Review the automatic package-installer confirmation. It lists the packages and repositories to add and any legacy files or folders it proposes to remove. Continue when these are the intended items.
6. Allow Unity to finish importing and compiling. If package installation does not finish automatically, open this project in VCC or ALCOM and add **Kawaii Posing Tool** and **Modular Avatar**. The shared **Unisaki Posing System** and **NDMF** are dependencies. `Optional-VCC-Links` contains the original repository shortcuts supplied with the product for Windows VCC users.
7. If a confirmation was cancelled, import the installer again when ready. You can also use its license-install command in **Tools > Unisaki Studio** while the activator is still present. In older builds this submenu is named **ゆにさきスタジオ**.
translations.952ab3fb036b1c5b: **Kawaii Posing Tool 3.2.0 with Unisaki Posing System 3.2.0.** This version is in development and has not been released. It adds thirty-language setup dialogs, Unity Inspector and menus, standard pose names, in-game menus, and offline documentation. The release date has not been set. Use the top-of-Inspector language selector to change the tool language. After publication, the installer will download these versions and their compatible dependencies from VPM repositories. Local release preparation does not publish those packages.
translations.a511a3ab974162c1: Kawaii Posing Tool includes the pose library, configuration tools, and avatar adjustment presets. The installer activates the product's existing local license; it does not require a new Gumroad license key field. Never post the installer files or license data in a public support request.
translations.6a4140f9fcf8696a: Language preferences are stored through Unity EditorPrefs for the current OS user and are shared across Unity projects on this computer. Without a saved preference, the installer follows the OS language; unsupported languages use English. Product licenses retain their existing storage: the current user's `Software/UnisakiStudio` registry key on Windows, and per-user license files on macOS/Linux. Changing a language does not remove a license.

1. In the **Hierarchy**, select the avatar with a **VRC Avatar Descriptor**, or one of its children. Use an avatar placed in a scene, rather than the Project window's prefab asset or Prefab Mode.
2. Right-click the avatar and choose **Unisaki Studio > Add Kawaii Posing**. If the installed build uses Japanese menus, choose **ゆにさきスタジオ > 可愛いポーズツール追加**.

translations.9df7843e8496a38b: The Inspector has three main tabs:
translations.be9c9eff2128305e:
| Tab | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| **Features** | In-game menu controls, optional behavior, breathing, icon options, and expression-parameter usage. |
| **Poses** | Enabled poses, category/search, ordering, adding animations, preview, details, and animation adjustment. |

translations.668fae5793d40c01: Enable only the menu controls you plan to use. For example, adding **Mirror** to the menu lets you switch mirroring in VRChat; it does not force every pose to stay mirrored.
translations.dac66ae03d2f290d: Kawaii Posing includes avatar presets and supported-pose IK. Three standard back-lying poses have side-lying motions already assigned: **Legs Out (足伸ばし)**, **Relaxed (リラックス)**, and **One Knee Up (膝立て)**. Use the matching preset and inspect each pose’s roll-over setting if you have edited or replaced these entries.
translations.67e242f06ec825c5: Presets are near the bottom of **Avatar Setup**. Search by avatar name, then apply a preset to replace the current pose settings. Save or back up adjustments before changing presets. A preset is a starting point: body proportions, outfits, and avatar modifications can still require manual corrections.
translations.9175b123d4e1a515: Use **Animation Adjustment** on a pose to preview and edit body/limb placement. Save the adjustment animation from that window when finished. Where supported, automatic hand and foot adjustment (IK) can be enabled globally and per pose. Baking the current IK result into an adjustment creates an adjustment animation and disables IK for that pose so you can refine it manually; the original source clip is kept.
translations.e15da49d2794570c: **Prevent reverse knee bending** has additional settings such as the minimum knee bend angle. Avatar-specific corrections are available only when corresponding correction data exists, and some corrections cannot be combined with pose IK.
translations.e69fbde91fce7241: **Use original standing, crouching and prone poses** detects motions from the avatar's Base layer during generation. **Use your own motions** opens separate import settings for each motion type. Choose one motion per type. Manual assignments take priority over automatic import for that type.
translations.e607ff56efa41bdf: Automatic import applies to the build copy. It does not write detected animations back into the scene's manual-assignment list or modify the original controllers. Clear a manual override for a type if you want automatic detection to handle it again. Custom Base layers and other locomotion systems may require individual adjustments.
translations.a2abdeb7b81b4ecc: Open your avatar's **Expressions** menu and enter **Kawaii Posing**. Choose a pose for each posture category you want to use. Selecting a pose and selecting a feature are separate actions.
translations.54fa51383a04a1d2:
- **Three-point VR:** lower or raise your head to change between standing, crouching/chair, floor-sitting, and lying postures. Adjust the height thresholds in the tool's settings menu if posture changes happen too early or too late.
- **Desktop:** use **C** to crouch and **Z** to lie down. If Z leaves you sitting, increase the lying-height threshold in the settings menu.
- **Lying front/back:** the tool uses face direction to select front- or back-lying. When both are selected, jumping in place can switch between them. Disable jump switching in Unity's **Features > Convenience** if you prefer; it adds no synced parameter cost.
- **Locks:** use head, arm, and foot locks as needed. Disable Gestures if you want the posed hand shape instead of controller gesture input.
- **Mirror:** flip a selected pose to face a friend or match a composition.
translations.4e5d1ed242d317ca: **Foot Height** adjusts the feet while keeping the head in place. Use it when your feet float or sink while the head is already at the right height.
translations.3c9d2ca82ea9281b: **Floor Height** moves the whole body, including the head. Use it for a sofa, bed, or raised surface, including furniture without a collider. On the shared system's current centered control, **50% is the original height**, 0% is 3 m below, and 100% is 3 m above. Return near 50% to end the offset. Older releases may have different control behavior; check the installed version and update the shared system together with the product.
translations.c7067b8f4e3f7447: Enable the **Photo Mode** menu entry in Unity before uploading. In VRChat, choose a pose, use **Distance** to move up to 3 m forward, and use **Direction** to turn the avatar. Lock Feet is optional while you arrange the shot. **Exit Photo Mode** resets distance/rotation and releases the foot lock.
translations.4b1071cdbb63c703: Photo Mode is local by default. To show the position and rotation to other people, enable **Sync Photo Mode** in Unity before uploading; this costs 16 synced bits. **Keep your head visible in Photo Mode** affects your own view and costs no synced bits.
translations.c226cdb39c8c1fb3: Breathing can be set per posture category in **Features > Convenience > Animate breathing**. Choose None, Weak, Medium, Strong, Rapid, or a custom breathing animation. The movement itself costs no synced bits. A menu toggle for breathing uses 1 bit.
translations.56d27e2f6c98b9e9: Roll over requires a supported lying pose and the **Roll Over** menu entry. Enable roll over for the pose and provide its side-lying animation when needed. In VRChat, choose that pose, enable roll over, and release head/neck lock. The head's sideways tilt then controls the roll. Normal MotionTime control is unavailable for that pose while roll over is used.
translations.f899f207728e8ee9: The three standard back-lying poses listed above include side-lying motions. Other poses require an appropriate motion and pose setting. Imported/custom presets can have different assignments.
translations.9c1d9eae0539ad04: In **Poses**, select a category or use the search tab. Search accepts original Japanese names and available translations. Open a pose's **Details** to edit its animation, icon, ordering, and timing options.
translations.2c4cd60737c88005: To add several animations, drag clips to the add area or select clips in the Project window and use the selected-clips import command. Duplicate references to the same clip are removed. Change the destination order in Details, or use the up/down controls.
translations.bad68e5c4e0ca386: **Preview** shows a pose in the Scene view without opening the full adjustment window. This lightweight preview does not run Modular Avatar or NDMF, so check the final avatar build for clothing, floor correction, and other build-time features.
translations.a0005b4a60905702: Pose icons generated from your avatar help identify poses, but generation takes time and can increase avatar data size. Reduce icon resolution to save space. Android builds do not generate pose icons. Regenerate icons after changing the avatar or outfit when required.
translations.126ad096501b9c5b: The Inspector shows the pose tools' contribution, not the entire avatar's total. Clothing and other systems can use additional parameter memory. Common settings shared by multiple pose tools are not counted twice. Custom configurations with many extra poses can need more pose-selection bits.
translations.94ad60ac38d64519:
| Feature | Additional synced bits |
| --- | ---: |
| Select Pose, minimum standard configuration | 8 |
| Mirror | 1 |
| Disable Gestures | 1 |
| Breathing movement | 0 |
| Breathing menu toggle | 1 |
| Foot Height | 8 |
| Floor Height | 8 |
| Photo Mode, local only | 0 |
| Sync Photo Mode | 16 |
| Keep your head visible in Photo Mode | 0 |
| Disable VRChat idle sway | 0 |
| Roll over | 10 |
translations.8e38def749eacdd0: Roll over shares 1 bit with the neck-direction posture correction: enabling both still uses 10 bits in total for those two features. The displayed usage in your installed version is the practical reference for your selected configuration.
translations.6821114682ad2934:
1. Back up the project and save your working scene.
2. In VCC or ALCOM, update **Kawaii Posing Tool** and the shared **Unisaki Posing System** together. Also keep required SDK, Modular Avatar, and NDMF versions compatible.

translations.7888738c09012544:
1. Extract the entire ZIP into a normal folder outside your Unity project.
2. Open the intended avatar project in Unity. Import `Installer/CoolPosing_Installer.unitypackage` using **Assets > Import Package > Custom Package**, or open the file with Unity.
3. Read the import and installation prompts. The license confirmation explains which product licenses will be installed. Use **Language...** (or **言語…**) in a confirmation dialog to change the installer language.
4. Confirm license installation. The license also covers the shared Unisaki Posing System used by this product. The installer can offer to remove its own setup files afterward; this cleanup does not remove the installed product license.
5. Review the automatic package-installer confirmation. It lists the packages and repositories to add and any legacy files or folders it proposes to remove. Continue when these are the intended items.
6. Allow Unity to finish importing and compiling. If package installation does not finish automatically, open this project in VCC or ALCOM and add **Cool Posing Tool** and **Modular Avatar**. The shared **Unisaki Posing System** and **NDMF** are dependencies. `Optional-VCC-Links` contains the original repository shortcuts supplied with the product for Windows VCC users.
7. If a confirmation was cancelled, import the installer again when ready. You can also use its license-install command in **Tools > Unisaki Studio** while the activator is still present. In older builds this submenu is named **ゆにさきスタジオ**.
translations.790187b65aa5e389: **Cool Posing Tool 1.2.0 with Unisaki Posing System 3.2.0.** This version is in development and has not been released. It adds thirty-language setup dialogs, Unity Inspector and menus, standard pose names, in-game menus, and offline documentation. The release date has not been set. Use the top-of-Inspector language selector to change the tool language. After publication, the installer will download these versions and their compatible dependencies from VPM repositories. Local release preparation does not publish those packages.
translations.cd35a97066714f25: Cool Posing Tool includes the pose library, configuration tools, and avatar adjustment presets. The installer activates the product's existing local license; it does not require a new Gumroad license key field. Never post the installer files or license data in a public support request.
translations.a7db8e8593d27872:
1. In the **Hierarchy**, select the avatar with a **VRC Avatar Descriptor**, or one of its children. Use an avatar placed in a scene, rather than the Project window's prefab asset or Prefab Mode.
2. Right-click the avatar and choose **Unisaki Studio > Add Cool Posing**. If the installed build uses Japanese menus, choose **ゆにさきスタジオ > カッコいいポーズツール追加**.
3. The tool is added inside the avatar. Its saved object name may remain **カッコいいポーズ** even when display labels are translated.
4. If a matching avatar preset is offered, apply it for a starting fit. Otherwise open **Avatar Setup** and choose a preset or adjust the poses yourself.
5. The installer may offer to prebuild. Prebuilding is optional; a normal avatar build also generates the required data. Reuse prebuilds to reduce later build times.
6. Select the tool object, choose the poses and features you want, then upload the avatar normally through the VRChat SDK.
translations.893f4ac7db85a756: Cool Posing includes presets for **トネール**, **狛乃**, **士堂**, and **真央**; these are the original avatar names used in the preset picker. Other Humanoid avatars can be adjusted manually. Automatic hand/foot adjustment is provided for 43 of the 50 included poses; the remaining seven use their pose adjustments. The included pose library does **not** include side-lying roll-over motions.
translations.37d7ce5459ec7863: Open your avatar's **Expressions** menu and enter **Cool Posing**. Choose a pose for each posture category you want to use. Selecting a pose and selecting a feature are separate actions.
translations.a551cc9a490836e6: Cool Posing’s included poses have no bundled roll-over motions. Supply suitable animations for the poses you want to use with roll over.
